sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Define the two-sided Z-transform of a sequence } \{x(n)\}.\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{By definition: } \delta(n) = 1 \text{ for } n=0, 0 \text{ otherwise}\)

(1 Mark)

\(Z[\delta(n)] = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \delta(n) z^{-n} = 1 \cdot z^{-0} + 0 + 0 + \cdots\)

(2 Mark)

sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Find the Z-transform of the unit sample sequence } \delta(n).\)

lq.ANSWER:
StepMarks

a) Definition:
For a sequence \(\{x(n)\}\) defined for \(n \ge 0\), the one-sided Z-transform is \(X(z) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} x(n) z^{-n}\).
The ROC is the set of all \(z\) in the complex plane for which this infinite sum converges.

(2 Marks)

b) Standard Transforms:
i) \(Z\{\delta(n)\} = 1\), ROC: Entire z-plane.
ii) \(Z\{u(n)\} = \frac{z}{z-1}\), ROC: \(|z| > 1\).
iii) \(Z\{a^n u(n)\} = \frac{z}{z-a}\), ROC: \(|z| > |a|\).
iv) \(Z\{n u(n)\} = \frac{z}{(z-1)^2}\), ROC: \(|z| > 1\).

(4 Marks: 1 each)

c) Given Sequence:
\(x(0)=2, x(1)=4, x(2)=1, x(3)=3\).
\(X(z) = \sum_{n=0}^{3} x(n) z^{-n} = 2z^0 + 4z^{-1} + 1z^{-2} + 3z^{-3} = 2 + \frac{4}{z} + \frac{1}{z^2} + \frac{3}{z^3}\).
Since it's a finite sum, the ROC is the entire z-plane except \(z = 0\).

(3 Marks)
